> **TARGET API / CONVERGING — not executable on the current runtime.**
> Library composition is proposed; runtime implementation is paused.

`Library` organizes reusable physical factories. This Chapter establishes only
project-catalog preparation, not a reusable physical declaration or component.
Lesson 7 adds the canonical Composite declaration.

The grounded LC is now familiar enough to reuse. In ordinary Python, a class
defines a kind of catalog and `components_library` is one instance of it; the
empty catalog below intentionally adds no new electrical circuit.

## Lesson 8.1 — Name the reusable catalog {#ch8-library}

First import the catalog base so the following declaration makes its ownership
boundary explicit.

```{python}
#| id: import-library-target
from scnsim import Library
```

Next define the complete, deliberately empty project catalog. It declares no
physical component; no factory belongs in this introductory lesson.

```{python}
#| id: define-empty-resonator-library-target
class ResonatorLibrary(Library):
    """Project-specific reusable resonator catalog."""
```

Create a catalog instance so later lessons can show its native inspection
surface and then add factories under the same Library boundary.

```{python}
#| id: instantiate-empty-resonator-library-target
components_library = ResonatorLibrary()
```

Inspect both the class contract and the catalog instance. Their help output
is the target documentation surface that Lesson 7 builds upon.

```{python}
#| id: inspect-empty-resonator-library-target
help(ResonatorLibrary)
help(components_library)
```

The catalog instance is intentionally empty: it establishes the catalog
boundary and native help surface before Lesson 7 rebuilds the clean-kernel
setup and adds a physical factory. The intended flow is `Library` subclass →
catalog instance → factory method → `ComponentInstance` → `plan.add(...)`.
